sources.title: Tagged interview note preserving word/DFS occurrence-count prompt

claims.text: The source preserves a word/DFS occurrence-count request but not the container, adjacency, reuse rule or occurrence identity.

Under the explicitly declared four-neighbor no-cell-reuse distinct-path-count contract, the exact recursive Java DFS matches independent bottom-up mask-state DP counts across fixed cases and 12,000 seeded random boards/words.

validation.command: compile exact Java candidate and differential-test against independent sparse-state DP oracle
validation.reported_stdout: PASS fixed-path-count=covered empty=covered no-reuse=covered random-vs-sparse-state-dp=12000 ragged=rejected oracle=bottom-up-mask-dp

boundary_tests.expected: distinct simple four-neighbor path counts match sparse-state DP

boundary_tests.case: 12,000 seeded random boards up to 3x3 and words up to length 7
boundary_tests.expected: recursive candidate equals independent bottom-up mask-state DP

findings: The preserved source is genuinely underspecified about the searched container, adjacency, cell reuse and the identity of one occurrence; the candidate explicitly preserves this uncertainty.
The rectangular four-neighbor distinct-simple-path model is labeled as a reference contract rather than claimed as recovered source semantics.

The recursive implementation has the required counting semantics: successful paths contribute one and sibling branches are accumulated; per-path used state is restored so different paths may reuse cells independently.
The answer distinguishes existence from counting and explains why global visited or success short-circuiting would be incorrect for the declared path-count contract.
A structurally separate bottom-up sparse DP over (mask,end-position) states passes fixed boundaries and 12,000 seeded random cases; malformed ragged grids are rejected consistently.
